Filtered learning hashes in state.json may grow unboundedly. FilteredLearningHashes accumulates hashes of every learning ever evaluated by the LLM filter, with no eviction policy. Over months of use this slice could grow to thousands of entries. Consider adding a TTL or max-size cap with LRU eviction.

Evaluate shifting more P1 work to opus — opus has 90.9% success rate vs sonnet's 37.5%. At ~$2/iteration for opus vs ~$0.46 for sonnet, opus is more cost-effective per completed bead. Consider adjusting model selection or adding a cost-effectiveness heuristic that factors in retry costs.

Investigate ATDD pre-pass problem — 13 iterations wasted on 'acceptance tests passed before implementation'. Either the acceptance tests aren't discriminating new behavior, the beads are already done and should be closed, or the test-before-implementation check has a bug. Audit the precheck/ATDD flow to find the root cause.

Verify ListWithLabel returns all statuses for epic bead counts — epic.go's getBeadCounts iterates ListWithLabel results counting open vs closed, but ListWithLabel calls bd list without --status filtering. If bd list defaults to only open beads, the closed count will always be 0 making progress reporting misleading. Need to verify bd behavior and potentially add --status all.

Evaluate whether medium-on-sonnet auto-escalation to opus is too aggressive — process.go:115-117 auto-escalates medium complexity beads from sonnet to opus. Combined with P1 already routing to opus in gromit.yaml, this effectively eliminates the intermediate tier. Everything goes to either haiku (tests) or opus (everything else). May be intentional given sonnet's 37.5% success rate, but should be a deliberate decision.
